definition: Christ, Paul and the early church, the apocalypse, the Church and Rome, and the Bible as scripture. Dick’s Christianity is the frame for most of his late theology, and the most heavily mentioned tradition in the Exegesis.
editorial_notes: Every mention is listed by subsection, with its lane, date and editorial status. Interpretive prose for this tradition is not yet written; see the subsections for the material.

subsections.label: Christ and Jesus
subsections.description: Christ as a person, as a cosmic principle, and as the figure whose return is awaited.

subsections.label: Paul, Acts and the early church
subsections.description: The Pauline letters, the Acts of the Apostles, and the Holy Spirit as Paraclete. Dick’s most sustained single reading of a biblical book is of Acts.

subsections.label: Apocalypse and the Second Advent
subsections.description: The Parousia, the apocalyptic books and the return of Christ, which Dick dates to his own lifetime.

subsections.label: The Church and Rome
subsections.description: Rome as the Empire of his 1974 vision, and the Church as institution, sacrament and authority.

subsections.label: Scripture and the Bible
subsections.description: The Bible as text, code and world. The full study is at /studies/bible/bible-in-pkd.
